policy: A named test is evidence of intent, not proof of a current result. Import TRX output from a recorded local or CI run; results retain run provenance and never overwrite the capability contract.
stalenessPolicy: A result from a different git revision is historical evidence only; it cannot satisfy a current strict-promotion review.
resultDiscoveryNote: Discovery here covers only the hand-curated TestResults directories, for a manual run of the collector. Run evidence is imported per run and ONLY per run: the full-tier GRADE row pdf-registry-outcomes calls scripts/check-pdf-capability-registry.sh --refresh-outcomes $LOG_DIR, which passes the trx of every test row in that run's ledger.jsonl (checkpointed rows included) as explicit --trx arguments, so nothing outside the run is unioned in; the snapshot moves only when someone adopts and commits that run's regenerated files (--adopt LOG_DIR). release-smoke (t2) results are deliberately NOT imported: the row is tier full only. Until 2026-09-05 this list also globbed logs/full-suite_*/**/*.trx and logs/release-smoke_*/**/*.trx, so the t0 gate's regeneration depended on whatever a previous run had left under logs/: the first manifest-driven full run reddened its own registry row (trxFiles 50 -> 74) and every t0 after it (#1366). Before 2026-09-04 it listed only TestResults, and the registry reported 7 of 964 modes as having a passing recorded contract while the suite was passing 10,332 tests - a plumbing defect being read as an evidence deficit.
devLoopRefreshNote: Wiring a registry check against Excise.Core.Tests/Excise.Rendering.Tests (the common case) does not need a full-tier run just to record the outcome. Run only the affected project(s), then scripts/collect-pdf-test-outcomes.py --merge --trx <fresh.trx> [--trx <fresh2.trx> ...]: it layers the new outcomes onto the committed snapshot and keeps every entry from a project it did not re-run (e.g. Excise.App.Tests, whose own unchunked run is 8-17 min, serial by design, #363), instead of a wholesale replace that would silently regress those untouched projects to 'no recorded outcome'. Without --merge the command still replaces wholesale -- correct for a full-tier run, where a removed test's stale outcome should disappear too. NEVER run an ad-hoc dotnet build/test command (even a small --filter, even with --no-build) while a tiered runner (t0/t1/full) is mid-run: any incremental build of Excise.Core/Excise.Rendering bumps their DLL mtimes past what a not-yet-reached downstream project (e.g. Excise.App.Tests) already copied, and its --no-build step correctly refuses as stale -- this cost a full App.Tests run + a wasted 40-minute t1 the day this note was added (2026-09-07).
